media.title: Listen Up Northwest Program 74
media.description:
Listen Up Northwest program 74: Quality of Life in the Schools
Listen Up! Northwest program 74

This week we look at how arts, music and strategic thinking transform the lives of students and teachers alike.

The Young Playwrights Program and Festival gives youth the chance to write plays and see their work performed. Learn more about the youth and educators behind its recent season. (Yuko Kodama, KBCS - Seattle, WA)

Garfield High Schoolâs jazz program wins national competitions and has performed at Lincoln Center.  Director Clarence Acox speaks about what makes it beat.  (Elaine Hayes, KBCS Seattle, WA) 

The Village Free School in Portland offers a program where students create their own curriculum and may even be involved in the contracts with their educators.  Julie Sabatier takes you to meet the educators and students at the school.  (Julie Sabatier, Destination DIY, Portland, OR)

Music by Blue Scholars, Garfield High School Jazz Band, Andy Combs and DJ B-Girl. Copy editor: Robbin Block. Host: Yuko Kodama.

media.title: Listen Up NW Program 47
media.description:
Listen Up! Northwest is a collaboratively produced radio magazine featuring stories of communities in action throughout the Northwest. Each broadcast highlights the work of skilled community radio producers and artists from our region, including Alaska, Alberta, British Columbia, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, and Washington.

In Listen Up Northwest program 47, we talk taxes, interviewing an anonymous war resister, one of many refusing to fund militarism with their tax dollars. (Sue Supriano, Steppinâ Out of Babylon, Eugene, OR). Also: a couple of Washington organizations are saying that wealthy corporations arenât paying their fair share of taxes.  Find out what the loopholes are. (David Griffith, Seattle, WA KBCS). Finally, commentary from Geov Parrish (KBCS, Seattle) on why we pay federal taxes. 

Music by DJ B-Girl and Blue Scholars.

Following up on last weekâs epic recap of 2011, this week we feature the MUSIC of 2011 including songs by Makana, Ras Ceylon, Hopie Spitshard, Rocky Rivera, Kiwi, Blue Scholars, Goh Nakamura, The Invisible Cities, The Little Bits, Senbei, and a rousing music video by Magnetic North and Taiyo Na featuring Jin.

We also honor the passing of activist and fellow radio producer, Yvette Hochberg, with a poem by Genny Lim.

Internet Archive item-level media expans.notes_continued_2026-10-22: A phrase-expanded catalog pass searched 41 exact Blue Scholars audio records, 6 movie records, 15 Sabzi audio records, and selected Geologic, Townfolk, video-title, and program-name queries. Eight additional program masters were acquired locally: six Listen Up Northwest episodes whose item descriptions credit Blue Scholars or DJ Sabzi, the Mother Jones 2006 broadcast whose description identifies an interview with Geologic, and the 2009 Off Air episode whose playlist places Blue Scholars “Hi-808” at 10:08. These add 320,164,428 bytes and are stored in ignored recovery/media/ia. Listen Up descriptions provide aggregate music credits, but this pass did not locate per-track segments or prove individual track timestamps. Mother Jones identifies Geologic but not the numbered segment containing him; the full MP3 is preserved rather than guessing. The item-level media manifest currently covers 27 source items and 35 selected files; together with explicit aliases for byte-identical legacy copies it maps all 37 files in recovery/media/ia. The separate 247,630,316-byte Seattle Channel MP4 remains cross-referenced by the Seattle Channel record in this report; the 100 MB media acquisition limit was not raised. The manifest script was improved to merge the saved phrase-query records and reconcile existing legacy filenames without redownloading. It was rerun with zero downloads on the final idempotence check; the only reported failure is the intentional over-limit Seattle Channel MP4 selection. Every manifest payload and all 20 Wikimedia Commons community-media source images passed byte/hash checks. All audio/video remains local-only; Archive.org item licenses do not clear the embedded music.
